solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Somehow got bag on sledge

indicators.note: somehow says the letters end up arranged in some unstated way, so they are to be shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone has managed, by some means, to get a bag onto a sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' shuffles the letters of GOT BAG ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a long, light sled used for sliding down snowy slopes, so it is a kind of sledge.

clue.text: Bunker perhaps where some turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: A golf question: in the bunker, where some balls surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses PART. On a golf course a bunker is a sand hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a bunker is a type of hazard, and a hazard in golf is also called a trap, as in sand trap.

clue.text: Introduce British group and popular first song

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of conspirators
in means fashionable or popular
top means first, as in top of the class
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A British band and its leading hit are being launched.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something into play is to introduce it into the action or start using it.

clue.text: Author, autobiographical at heart, penning worthiest novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new, rearranged
at heart points to the middle letters of the long word, its centre

explanation.surface: A writer, autobiographical deep down, writing the worthiest novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' gives GR from the middle of autobiographical; 'penning' brings those in with WORTHIEST, and 'novel' shuffles all eleven letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter is an author who writes books, often memoirs, published under someone else's name.

clue.text: Wily like ancient king, leader in Egypt

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian boy king

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cunning ruler likened to a pharaoh, first in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and wily both describe someone shrewd and clever at getting an advantage.

clue.text: Notice small vessel

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

explanation.surface: Someone catches sight of a little container.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, both verbs meaning to catch sight of.

clue.text: What father of the bride may do, slamming poor OAP's taste

definitions.text: What father of the bride may do

indicators.note: slamming here means criticising harshly, battering the words so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: At a wedding a bride's father criticises a pensioner's dreadful taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slamming' rearranges POOR OAP'S TASTE. OAP is British for old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding reception the bride's father traditionally makes a speech and asks guests to raise their glasses.

clue.text: Prize certain to be given after short walk

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, missing its last letter

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A guaranteed prize will be awarded following a brief stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the walking word, and 'to be given after' sets the certain word behind it; 'Prize' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly, which is to treasure it.

clue.text: I turn to follow a male friend

indicators.note: to follow says the pieces before it come after the ones named later, a and male

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone takes their turn after a man who is their friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, familiar in English as a casual term of address.

clue.text: Couple in book holding pig back

indicators.note: holding says the book contains the next piece

parts.note: a tome is a book, usually a large one

indicators.note: back says the word for the pig is read the other way round

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair of characters appear in a book that features a pig coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the female pig, and 'holding' puts it inside the big book.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, as a couple is two people together.

clue.text: Working out initially sensible following PE

indicators.note: following says the sensible word comes after PE
initially means the first letter of the word next to it

parts.note: rational means sensible, reasonable

explanation.surface: Working out sensibly after a physical education class.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school gym lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Something operational is in working order, up and running.

clue.text: Visit kennels in decline

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase means to go and see some hounds, as at a kennels or dog track
the idiom means to deteriorate badly, to fall into ruin

explanation.surface: Visiting the dog kennels marks a sad downturn in someone's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally means heading off to see some dogs, and idiomatically means going to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something deteriorating, and taken literally it describes a trip to see hounds.

clue.text: Settled under tree to get medical attention

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the settled word below the tree

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
staid means settled, steady and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone resting beneath a tree receives emergency treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the initial medical help given to the injured before professional treatment.

clue.text: Pass by one rig at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat sails past a single oil rig out in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the letters of ONE RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone by is to take no notice of them, which is to disregard them.

clue.text: Rush job

definitions.meaning: to rush headlong, out of control, as a speeding vehicle does
a job in the sense of one's profession or line of work

explanation.surface: A hasty assignment needing to be done quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to hurtle along wildly; as a noun it means a working life or profession.

clue.text: Canny, mean-spirited woman and daughter

parts.note: a shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging woman

explanation.surface: A shrewish mother and her daughter are sharp operators.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny and shrewd both mean having sharp practical judgement.

clue.text: Curt treatment of Republican wearing mini dress

parts.note: a mini skirt or dress is short

indicators.note: wearing means the Republican has the dress on, sitting inside it

parts.note: a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: A Republican in a skimpy mini dress gets an abrupt dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mini dress' reads as one garment, but it splits into a word for brief and a simple dress, with 'wearing' putting the Republican inside the dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift is brusque, dismissive handling, the curt treatment given to something not taken seriously.

clue.text: Game is extremely pricey

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the letters at each end

explanation.surface: A sport that costs a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: I-spy is a children's guessing game played by naming something seen that starts with a given letter.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a children's guessing game, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Free lager distributed after a time

indicators.note: after says the jumbled lager comes behind a and time
distributed means spread around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Free beer is handed round after some time has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped prisoner at large is free, still not recaptured.

clue.text: Approaches some within earshot

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something gets nearer, close enough for some people to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach something is to draw close to it, to come nearer.

clue.text: Some time in confused state, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says what precedes is only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a daze is a stunned, confused state

explanation.surface: Someone has spent a while in a muddled condition, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Days is a stretch of time, as in 'it took days'.

clue.text: Hero-worshipping adroitly revised

indicators.note: revised means altered or rewritten, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Fan adoration has been cleverly edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges ADROITLY; the definition is a noun use of the hyphenated word, the worshipping of heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive adoration of a person, as hero-worship is the excessive admiration of a hero.
